senses.def: every one of two or more things, considered separately
ex: Each student has a book.

senses.def: every one of a group
ex: Each of them is different.

mistake.wrong: Each of the students have a book.
mistake.right: Each of the students has a book.
mistake.note: Each takes a singular verb.

senses.def: wanting to do something very much
ex: She is eager to learn.

senses.def: a large bird with excellent eyesight that hunts
ex: An eagle flew over the mountains.

senses.def: to get money for work
ex: He earns £30,000 a year.

senses.def: to get something because of what you have done
ex: She earned our respect.

mistake.wrong: He wins a lot of money.
mistake.right: He earns a lot of money.
mistake.note: Use earn for money from work; win is for competitions.

senses.def: the money that a person or company earns
ex: Average earnings have risen.

senses.def: the planet we live on (also Earth)
ex: The Earth moves round the sun.

senses.def: soil
ex: The earth was dry.

senses.def: the quality of being easy
ex: She passed the exam with ease.

senses.def: to make pain or problems less severe
ex: The medicine eased the pain.

senses.def: without difficulty
ex: She easily won the race.

senses.def: by far
ex: It's easily the best film.

senses.def: in or towards the east
ex: The east coast is warmer.

senses.def: towards the east
ex: Drive east for two miles.

senses.def: the direction where the sun rises
ex: The wind comes from the east.

senses.def: in or from the east of a place
ex: She lives in eastern Spain.

senses.def: not difficult, needing little effort
ex: The test was easy.

senses.def: comfortable and relaxed
ex: She has an easy life.

senses.def: to put food in your mouth and swallow it
ex: I eat breakfast at seven.

senses.def: if the tide ebbs, the sea moves away from the land
ex: The tide ebbed slowly.

senses.def: to slowly become weaker
ex: Her strength began to ebb.

senses.def: behaving in a strange or unusual way
ex: He is an eccentric old man.

senses.def: a person who behaves in an unusual way
ex: The artist was a lovable eccentric.

senses.def: a sound that is repeated when it hits a surface
ex: We heard an echo in the cave.

senses.def: if a sound echoes, it is heard again after it hits a surface
ex: Her voice echoed in the hall.

senses.def: connected with money, trade and industry
ex: The country faces economic problems.

senses.def: the system of money, trade and industry of a country
ex: The economy is growing.

mistake.note: The subject is economics; economy means a country's system of money.

senses.def: a feeling of extreme happiness
ex: She danced with ecstasy.

senses.def: extremely happy
ex: The fans were ecstatic after the win.

senses.def: the outer line of something
ex: He stood at the edge of the cliff.

senses.def: an advantage over others
ex: The team has an edge over its rivals.

senses.def: a large impressive building
ex: The bank is a grand edifice.

senses.def: a change made to a piece of writing
ex: I made a quick edit to the report.

senses.def: to correct and improve a piece of writing or video
ex: She edited the article.

senses.def: a particular form of a book or newspaper published at one time
ex: The second edition has new photos.

senses.def: an article in a newspaper giving the opinion of the editor
ex: The editorial criticised the plan.

senses.def: having received a good education
ex: She is an educated woman.

senses.def: the process of teaching and learning, especially at school
ex: She has a good education.

senses.def: a change that is caused by something
ex: The medicine had a strange effect.

mistake.note: Affect is the verb; effect is the noun.

senses.def: producing the result you want
ex: This is an effective way to learn.

senses.def: in a way that produces the result you want
ex: The team worked effectively.

senses.def: in fact
ex: It effectively ended the discussion.

senses.def: working well without wasting time or energy
ex: The new machine is more efficient.

senses.def: physical or mental energy used to do something
ex: She put a lot of effort into her studies.

senses.def: your idea of how good or important you are
ex: His success boosted his ego.

senses.def: used after a negative to mean also
ex: I don't like fish. I don't like meat either.

senses.def: used with or to show two possibilities
ex: You can either walk or take a bus.

senses.def: one or the other of two
ex: You can use either door.

senses.def: one of two things or people
ex: Either would be fine.

mistake.note: Use either, not too, to add a negative idea.

senses.def: complicated and with many parts
ex: They made elaborate plans.

senses.def: to give more details about something
ex: Can you elaborate on that?

senses.def: a rubber-like material that stretches
ex: The skirt has elastic at the waist.

senses.def: able to stretch and return to its shape
ex: The cloth is elastic.

senses.def: the ability to stretch and return to the original shape
ex: The cloth lost its elasticity.

senses.def: extremely happy and excited
ex: She was elated at the news.

senses.def: a feeling of great happiness
ex: He jumped with elation.

senses.def: the part in the middle of your arm where it bends
ex: She leaned on her elbows.

senses.def: to choose someone by voting
ex: They elected her president.

senses.def: an event where people vote to choose a leader
ex: The election takes place in May.

senses.def: using or connected with electricity
ex: Check the electrical wires.

mistake.note: Electrical describes things related to electricity in general; electric describes something powered by it.

senses.def: a person whose job is to install and repair electrical equipment
ex: We called an electrician.

senses.def: a form of energy used for light, heat and machines
ex: The house has no electricity.

senses.def: a metal part through which electricity enters or leaves
ex: The electrodes were placed in the liquid.

senses.def: using small electrical parts, like chips
ex: He sells electronic equipment.

senses.def: equipment such as televisions, computers and phones
ex: The shop sells electronics.

senses.def: the quality of being graceful and stylish
ex: She dressed with elegance.

senses.def: graceful and attractive
ex: She wore an elegant dress.

senses.def: one part of something
ex: Trust is a key element of friendship.

senses.def: a basic chemical substance
ex: Gold is an element.

senses.def: to lift or raise something
ex: The platform elevates the speaker.

senses.def: to make something better or more important
ex: Education elevates people.

senses.def: height above sea level
ex: The village is at an elevation of 800 metres.

senses.def: a machine that carries people up and down in a building (American; British: lift)
ex: Take the elevator to the fifth floor.

senses.def: having the right to do something
ex: Only adults are eligible to vote.

senses.def: to remove something completely
ex: The plan will eliminate waste.

senses.def: to stop a person or team from continuing in a competition
ex: Our team was eliminated in the first round.

senses.def: the best or most powerful group of people
ex: Only the elite can join the club.

senses.def: other, different or more
ex: Would you like anything else?

mistake.note: Use else after question words and any-, some-, no- words.

senses.def: difficult to find, catch or achieve
ex: Success proved elusive.

senses.def: to begin something new, or to get on a ship
ex: She embarked on a new career.

senses.def: to make someone feel ashamed or awkward
ex: His jokes embarrassed her.

senses.def: feeling ashamed or awkward
ex: I felt embarrassed when I forgot his name.

senses.def: making you feel ashamed or awkward
ex: It was an embarrassing mistake.

mistake.note: -ed describes how you feel; -ing describes the thing that causes the feeling.

senses.def: a feeling of being ashamed or awkward
ex: She blushed with embarrassment.

senses.def: the offices of an ambassador and their staff in a foreign country
ex: She went to the embassy to get a visa.

senses.def: a perfect example of a quality or idea
ex: She is the embodiment of kindness.

senses.def: to be a perfect example of a quality or idea
ex: He embodies the spirit of the team.

senses.def: the act of holding someone close in your arms
ex: They greeted each other with a warm embrace.

senses.def: to come out from a hidden place
ex: The sun emerged from the clouds.

senses.def: to become known
ex: New facts have emerged.

senses.def: a sudden dangerous event that needs quick action
ex: Call 999 in an emergency.

senses.def: the state of being famous and respected
ex: He rose to eminence as a doctor.

senses.def: famous and respected
ex: She is an eminent scientist.

senses.def: a strong feeling such as love, anger or fear
ex: She could not hide her emotion.

senses.def: connected with feelings
ex: He needs emotional support.

senses.def: showing strong feelings
ex: She became emotional.

senses.def: in a way that relates to feelings
ex: He was emotionally tired.

senses.def: a man who rules an empire
ex: The emperor lived in a palace.

senses.def: special importance or attention given to something
ex: The course places emphasis on speaking.
Inversion adds emphasis and a formal tone.

mistake.wrong: He emphasized on the importance of practice.
mistake.right: He emphasized the importance of practice. / He put emphasis on the importance of practice.
mistake.note: The verb emphasize has no preposition. The noun emphasis takes on.

senses.def: a group of countries ruled by one ruler or government
ex: The Roman Empire was huge.

senses.def: to pay someone to work for you
ex: The company employs 500 people.

senses.def: to use something
ex: The police employed new methods.

mistake.wrong: She is employed from a bank.
mistake.right: She is employed by a bank.
mistake.note: Use employed by a company.

senses.def: a person who is paid to work for a company
ex: The company has 200 employees.

senses.def: a person or company that pays people to work
ex: My employer offers training.

senses.def: having a paid job
ex: He is looking for employment.

senses.def: with nothing inside
ex: The fridge is empty.

senses.def: to try to be like someone you admire
ex: He tried to emulate his hero.

senses.def: an unexpected meeting
ex: It was a chance encounter.

senses.def: to meet or experience something unexpectedly
ex: We encountered problems on the way.

senses.def: giving you hope or confidence
ex: The results are encouraging.

senses.def: the last part of something
ex: I loved the end of the film.

senses.def: the tip or extremity of something
ex: He stood at the end of the line.

senses.def: to stop, or to make something stop
ex: The film ends at ten.

senses.def: seeming to have no end
ex: The road seemed endless.

senses.def: without stopping
ex: They talked endlessly.

senses.def: public support or approval
ex: The film received a big endorsement.

senses.def: the ability to continue despite difficulty
ex: Running a marathon needs endurance.

senses.def: to accept pain or difficulty without giving up
ex: They endured years of hardship.

senses.def: a person who hates or fights you
ex: He made many enemies.

senses.def: the ability to be active, or power used for heat and light
ex: I have no energy today.

mistake.right: I need a lot of energy.
mistake.note: Energy is uncountable, so use a lot of or much.

senses.def: to make sure that a rule is obeyed
ex: Police enforce the law.

senses.def: to attract and keep someone's interest
ex: The teacher engaged the class.

senses.def: to take part in something
ex: They engaged in conversation.

senses.def: having agreed to marry someone
ex: They are engaged to be married.

senses.def: busy (e.g. a phone line)
ex: The line is engaged.

senses.def: an agreement to marry
ex: Their engagement was announced.

senses.def: an arrangement to do something at a fixed time
ex: I have a prior engagement.

senses.def: a machine that produces power to make something move
ex: The car engine is noisy.

senses.def: the design and building of machines, roads and structures
ex: He studied engineering.

senses.def: a man from England
ex: The Englishman ordered tea.

senses.def: to improve the quality of something
ex: Exercise enhances your mood.

senses.def: very much
ex: I enjoyed it enormously.

senses.def: to the necessary degree
ex: She is old enough to drive.

senses.def: as much as is needed
ex: We have enough chairs.

senses.def: as much as is needed
ex: Do you have enough?

mistake.wrong: I have enough money for buy it.
mistake.right: I have enough money to buy it.
mistake.note: After enough use to + verb, not for + verb.

senses.def: to make certain that something happens
ex: Please ensure the door is locked.

senses.def: to go into a place
ex: She entered the room.

senses.def: to put information into a computer
ex: Enter your password.

mistake.note: Enter takes a direct object, with no preposition.

senses.def: a company or business
ex: He runs a small enterprise.

senses.def: willingness to try new things
ex: She showed great enterprise.

senses.def: to give people enjoyment
ex: The clown entertained the children.

senses.def: to invite guests and give them food
ex: They entertain friends every Friday.

senses.def: enjoyable and amusing
ex: It was an entertaining show.

senses.def: strong interest and excitement
ex: She spoke with great enthusiasm.

senses.def: very interested and excited about something
ex: He is enthusiastic about football.

senses.def: whole or complete
ex: I slept the entire day.

senses.def: completely
ex: I entirely agree.

senses.def: a door or gate where you go in
ex: Meet me at the entrance.

senses.def: the act of coming into a place
ex: His entrance surprised us.

senses.def: a person who starts a business
ex: She is a young entrepreneur.

senses.def: the act of going into a place
ex: Entry is free.

senses.def: a single item in a list
ex: Look up the entry in the dictionary.

senses.def: the air, water and land in which people live
ex: We must protect the environment.

senses.def: the conditions in which you live or work
ex: It's a friendly working environment.

senses.def: connected with the natural world
ex: Pollution is an environmental problem.

senses.def: lasting for a very short time
ex: Fame can be ephemeral.

senses.def: one programme in a series
ex: I watched two episodes last night.

senses.def: an event in a longer story
ex: It was a sad episode in his life.

senses.def: the same in amount, size or value
ex: All people are equal.

senses.def: a person of the same status as another
ex: She treats everyone as her equal.

senses.def: to be the same as
ex: Two plus two equals four.

senses.def: to the same degree
ex: Both players are equally good.

senses.def: a statement showing that two quantities are equal
ex: Solve the equation.

senses.def: a state in which opposing forces are balanced
ex: The economy reached equilibrium.

senses.def: the tools and machines needed for a job
ex: The gym has modern equipment.

mistake.note: Equipment is uncountable and has no plural form.

senses.def: a period of history
ex: It was the era of silent films.

senses.def: a sudden throwing out of lava and ash from a volcano
ex: The eruption covered the town in ash.

senses.def: the act of getting free from a place or danger
ex: The prisoner made a daring escape.

senses.def: to get away from a place or danger
ex: The cat escaped from the house.

senses.def: more than usual or more than others; in particular
ex: I love fruit, especially mangoes.
It is especially cold in January.

senses.def: the most important quality of something that makes it what it is
ex: The essence of good teaching is patience.
Honesty is the essence of a good friendship.

senses.def: a strong liquid taken from a plant, used for flavour or smell
ex: Add a few drops of vanilla essence.

senses.def: completely necessary; that you must have
ex: Water is essential for life.
It is essential to book early.

senses.def: used to talk about the most important part of something
ex: The two plans are essentially the same.
She is essentially a shy person.

senses.def: the act of starting something such as a company or system
ex: The establishment of the school took two years.

senses.def: a business, school or other organisation, or the building it uses
ex: This is a well-known dining establishment.

senses.def: a large area of land with a big house, owned by one person or family
ex: They own a large estate in the country.

senses.def: a group of houses or factories built together in one area
ex: They live on a housing estate near the school.

senses.def: to say what you think an amount or cost will be, using the information you have
ex: We estimate that the trip will cost £500.
Experts estimate the building is 200 years old.

senses.def: a judgement about the size, cost or amount of something, not exact
ex: Can you give me an estimate for the repairs?
A rough estimate is ten thousand people.

senses.def: calculated roughly, not exactly
ex: The estimated cost is two million pounds.
The estimated arrival time is six o'clock.

senses.def: to cut a design into a hard surface, especially metal or glass
ex: Their names were etched into the stone.
He etched a pattern on the glass.

senses.def: to be fixed strongly in your memory
ex: The scene is etched on my memory.

senses.def: continuing for ever; without an end
ex: Many people believe in eternal life.
She promised him eternal love.

senses.def: for ever; without ever ending
ex: I will be eternally grateful for your help.
The flame burns eternally.

senses.def: time that has no end
ex: Some people believe the soul lives for eternity.

senses.def: a very long time, or what feels like a very long time
ex: We waited an eternity for the bus.

senses.def: relating to what is right and wrong in behaviour
ex: Doctors face difficult ethical decisions.
The company has an ethical approach to business.

senses.def: relating to a group of people who share the same culture, language or origin
ex: The city has many different ethnic communities.
Ethnic minorities make up ten per cent of the population.

senses.def: the set of beliefs and values that guide a group or organisation
ex: The school has a strong ethos of respect.
Teamwork is central to the company's ethos.

senses.def: a mild or polite word used instead of a more direct one that may upset people
ex: "Passed away" is a euphemism for "died".
He used a euphemism to avoid sounding rude.

senses.def: a feeling of extreme happiness and excitement
ex: The fans were filled with euphoria after the win.
A wave of euphoria swept the crowd.

senses.def: feeling extremely happy and excited
ex: She felt euphoric when she heard the news.
The euphoric crowd ran onto the pitch.

senses.def: to move people out of a dangerous place to a safe one
ex: Thousands of people were evacuated before the storm.
They evacuated the building after the fire alarm.

senses.def: the act of moving people out of a dangerous place
ex: The evacuation of the town took several hours.
An evacuation was ordered because of the flood.

senses.def: to think carefully about something to decide how good or useful it is
ex: Teachers evaluate students' work every term.
We need to evaluate the risks first.

senses.def: the process of judging how good, useful or successful something is
ex: The course ends with a final evaluation.
A full evaluation of the project is needed.

senses.def: used to show that something is surprising or extreme
ex: Even my little brother can do it.
She didn't even say hello.

senses.def: used to make a comparison stronger
ex: Today is even hotter than yesterday.

senses.def: flat and smooth, with no parts higher than others
ex: The table needs an even surface.

senses.def: equal in amount or score
ex: The score is even at two goals each.

senses.def: able to be divided exactly by two
ex: Four, six and eight are even numbers.

mistake.right: Even though I was tired, I went.
mistake.note: Do not confuse even (adverb) with even though, which joins two clauses; even if is used for unreal situations.

senses.def: in the end, after a long time or a lot of effort
ex: We eventually found a hotel.
He eventually learned to swim.

mistake.wrong: Eventually I may go to Paris next year.
mistake.right: I may possibly go to Paris next year.
mistake.note: eventually does not mean 'possibly'; Arabic speakers sometimes use it like the French 'éventuellement'.

senses.def: at any time; used in questions and negatives
ex: Have you ever been to Egypt?
Nobody ever calls me.

senses.def: used after a superlative to emphasise it
ex: This is the best film ever.

mistake.wrong: I have ever been to London.
mistake.right: I have never been to London.
mistake.note: Use ever in questions and with negatives or superlatives, not in simple positive statements.

senses.def: continuing for ever or for a very long time
ex: They promised everlasting friendship.
The story gave her everlasting fame.

senses.def: used with a singular noun to mean all the people or things in a group
ex: Every student has a book.
I walk to school every day.

senses.def: used to say how often something happens
ex: The bus comes every ten minutes.

mistake.note: every is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb, unlike Arabic كل with a plural.

senses.def: every person in a group
ex: Everybody is here.
Everybody loves a good story.

mistake.note: everybody takes a singular verb, even though it means many people.

senses.def: every person in a group
ex: Everyone likes pizza.
Hello, everyone!

mistake.note: everyone takes a singular verb.

senses.def: all things; all of something
ex: I packed everything last night.
Everything is ready.

senses.def: facts or signs that show something is true
ex: There is no evidence that he was there.
The police found new evidence.

mistake.right: We found a lot of evidence.
mistake.note: evidence is uncountable, so it has no plural form; say a piece of evidence.

senses.def: in a way that is easy to see or understand
ex: He was evidently tired after the long trip.
Evidently, nobody had told her.

senses.def: very bad and cruel; causing harm to others
ex: The film has an evil king.
He had an evil plan.

senses.def: things that are very bad and harmful, or the force that causes them
ex: The story is about good against evil.

senses.def: the slow development of something into a different or better form
ex: The evolution of the phone has been fast.

senses.def: the process by which living things change over millions of years
ex: Darwin explained evolution by natural selection.

senses.def: to develop slowly into a different or more advanced form
ex: Languages evolve over time.
The small shop evolved into a large company.

senses.def: completely correct in every detail
ex: What is the exact time?
I need the exact address.

senses.def: to demand and get something from someone, often by force
ex: The company exacted a high price from its workers.

senses.def: used to say that something is completely correct or accurate
ex: It is exactly three o'clock.
That is exactly what I mean.

senses.def: used to agree strongly with someone
ex: "So you want to leave?" "Exactly!"

senses.def: to say that something is bigger, better or worse than it really is
ex: Don't exaggerate; it wasn't that bad.
He exaggerated the size of the fish.

senses.def: having a very high position or rank, or very great and admired
ex: He holds an exalted position in the government.
She mixes with people of exalted rank.

senses.def: a formal test of what you know, usually written
ex: She passed her final examination.
The examination lasts two hours.

senses.def: a careful look at something or someone to find out more about it
ex: The doctor gave him a full examination.

senses.def: to look at something carefully to learn more about it
ex: The doctor examined my throat.
Scientists examined the soil samples.

senses.def: to test what a student knows
ex: She was examined in maths and science.

senses.def: a person who sets or marks an exam or tests someone's ability
ex: The examiner asked me three questions.
The examiners mark the papers in June.

senses.def: used before a statement that shows an exception to what you just said
ex: I know nothing about him, except that he lives here.

senses.def: not including; apart from
ex: Everyone came except Tom.
The shop is open every day except Sunday.

mistake.note: Do not confuse except (not including) with expect (think something will happen).

senses.def: a person or thing that is not included in a rule or general statement
ex: Most rules have exceptions.
With the exception of Ali, everyone came.

senses.def: unusually good or great
ex: She is an exceptional student.
The food was of exceptional quality.

senses.def: unusual and happening only rarely
ex: Schools close only in exceptional circumstances.

senses.def: to a very unusual or high degree
ex: The weather was exceptionally hot.
He is an exceptionally talented player.

senses.def: more than is needed, allowed or usual
ex: Pay extra for excess luggage.
Eating in excess is bad for you.

senses.def: more than is necessary or reasonable
ex: The car was travelling at excessive speed.
He thinks the price is excessive.

senses.def: the act of giving one thing and getting another
ex: We had a quick exchange of gifts.
He gave me a book in exchange for a pen.

senses.def: the act of changing money into another currency
ex: The exchange rate is good today.

senses.def: to give something and get something similar from another person
ex: We exchanged phone numbers.
She exchanged the shirt for a bigger one.

senses.def: a feeling of being happy and full of energy about something
ex: The children screamed with excitement.
There was great excitement before the match.

senses.def: very expensive and only for rich or special people
ex: They stayed at an exclusive hotel.
It is a very exclusive club.

senses.def: not shared with anyone else
ex: The magazine has an exclusive interview with the singer.

senses.def: only; not including anything or anyone else
ex: The shop sells exclusively organic food.
This room is used exclusively by staff.

senses.def: a reason you give to explain a mistake or to avoid doing something
ex: What is your excuse for being late?
He always has an excuse.

senses.def: to forgive a small mistake or bad behaviour
ex: Please excuse my bad handwriting.
Excuse me, where is the station?

senses.def: to say that someone does not have to do something
ex: She was excused from the lesson.

mistake.wrong: I made an excuse for being late.
mistake.note: An excuse is a reason you offer for a fault; it does not mean 'apology'.

senses.def: to do a plan, order or action
ex: The team executed the plan perfectly.
The program executes the commands in order.

senses.def: to kill someone as a legal punishment
ex: The prisoner was executed in 1950.

senses.def: the act of killing someone as a legal punishment
ex: The execution took place at dawn.

senses.def: the act of doing a plan or action
ex: The execution of the plan was perfect.

senses.def: having the power to make decisions and manage a company or country
ex: She is the executive director of the charity.
The executive committee met on Monday.

senses.def: a senior person in a company who makes important decisions
ex: He is a senior executive at a bank.

senses.def: to use power, influence or effort to make something happen
ex: Parents exert a strong influence on their children.
Don't exert too much pressure on him.

senses.def: the gas or fumes that come out of a vehicle's engine
ex: Exhaust fumes pollute the city air.
The car's exhaust pipe is broken.

senses.def: to make someone very tired
ex: The long walk exhausted us.

senses.def: to use all of something so that nothing is left
ex: We have exhausted our supply of water.

senses.def: extremely tired
ex: I was exhausted after the long flight.
She looked exhausted.

senses.def: making you feel extremely tired
ex: It was an exhausting day at work.
Looking after a baby can be exhausting.

senses.def: a state of being extremely tired
ex: He collapsed from exhaustion.
Exhaustion made it hard to think.

senses.def: to show something in a public place such as a museum
ex: Her paintings will be exhibited in Paris.

senses.def: to show a feeling, quality or sign clearly
ex: The patient exhibited signs of stress.

senses.def: making you feel very happy, excited and full of energy
ex: Skiing down the mountain was exhilarating.
It was an exhilarating experience.

senses.def: a situation in which you must live outside your own country, often for political reasons
ex: The king lived in exile for ten years.
He was sent into exile.

senses.def: to be real or present in the world
ex: Dinosaurs no longer exist.
Do ghosts really exist?

senses.def: to live, especially in difficult conditions
ex: They exist on very little money.

mistake.note: exist is never used in the passive; it means 'to be present', so no 'is existed'.

senses.def: the state of being real or alive
ex: Scientists are looking for proof of the animal's existence.
The company came into existence in 1990.

senses.def: a way of living
ex: He led a lonely existence.

senses.def: present now, not new or planned
ex: We plan to improve the existing system.
Existing customers get a discount.

senses.def: a door or way out of a building or place
ex: The fire exit is on the left.
Take the second exit at the roundabout.

senses.def: the act of leaving a place
ex: She made a quick exit.

senses.def: to go out of a place
ex: Please exit by the rear door.
Press this key to exit the program.

senses.def: a situation in which many people leave a place at the same time
ex: There was a mass exodus from the city at the weekend.
War caused an exodus of refugees.

senses.def: a ceremony to force an evil spirit to leave a person or place
ex: The priest performed an exorcism.
The film is about a young girl and an exorcism.

senses.def: a person who performs a ceremony to drive out evil spirits
ex: The family called an exorcist to the old house.

senses.def: unusual and interesting because it comes from a distant or foreign place
ex: We saw exotic birds in the jungle.
She loves exotic fruits like papaya.

senses.def: to become larger or make something larger
ex: The company plans to expand abroad.
Metal expands when it is heated.

senses.def: the process of becoming larger or making something larger
ex: The airport needs an expansion.
There has been rapid expansion in the city.

senses.def: to think that something will happen or someone will come
ex: I expect it will rain tomorrow.
We are expecting guests tonight.

senses.def: to believe someone should do something
ex: The teacher expects us to be on time.

senses.def: to be going to have a baby
ex: She is expecting a baby in May.

mistake.wrong: I am expecting you since one hour.
mistake.right: I have been waiting for you for an hour.
mistake.note: Use wait, not expect, when you are staying somewhere until someone comes; expect means 'think it will happen'.

senses.def: a belief that something will happen or that someone should do something
ex: The film did not live up to my expectations.
She has high expectations of her students.

senses.def: thought to be likely to happen or arrive
ex: The expected result was a win.
Heavy rain is expected tonight.

senses.def: to make a process happen more quickly
ex: We paid extra to expedite the delivery.
Officials promised to expedite the visa request.

senses.def: a long, organised journey for a special purpose, such as exploring
ex: The team went on an expedition to the Arctic.
They led a scientific expedition.

senses.def: the money you spend on something
ex: Running a car is a big expense.
The trip was a great expense for us.

senses.def: money spent on things for your job that your employer pays back
ex: The company pays all travel expenses.

senses.def: [U] knowledge or skill that you get from doing a job or activity
ex: An internship helps you gain experience.
Do you have any experience of working with children?
She has ten years' experience in marketing.

senses.def: [C] something that happens to you that affects how you feel
ex: Living abroad was an amazing experience.
We had some strange experiences on that trip.

mistake.wrong: I have three years experiences in sales.
mistake.right: I have three years' experience in sales.
mistake.note: When it means خبرة, experience is uncountable. Use the plural only for تجارب (events).

senses.def: having skill or knowledge because you have done something for a long time
ex: She is an experienced teacher.
We need someone experienced in sales.

senses.def: a scientific test done to find out something or prove an idea
ex: We did an experiment in chemistry class.
The experiment proved his theory.

senses.def: an action in which you try something new to see what happens
ex: Cooking is a fun experiment for her.

senses.def: to try new ideas or methods to see what happens
ex: Chefs experiment with new flavours.
Scientists experiment on mice.

senses.def: a person with special skill or great knowledge of a subject
ex: He is an expert in computers.
Ask an expert for advice.

senses.def: having or showing great skill or knowledge
ex: I need expert advice on taxes.
She is an expert cook.

senses.def: to come to an end, usually when a fixed time has finished
ex: My passport expires next month.
The offer expires on Friday.

senses.def: to make something clear or easy to understand by giving details
ex: Can you explain this rule to me?
He explained why he was late.

mistake.right: Can you explain this to me?
mistake.note: explain + thing + to + person. Never explain me.

senses.def: details or reasons that make something clear
ex: The teacher gave a clear explanation.
He had no explanation for his mistake.

senses.def: to burst loudly and violently, causing damage
ex: The bomb exploded at noon.
The gas pipe exploded.

senses.def: to suddenly show strong feeling, especially anger
ex: He exploded with rage when he saw the damage.

senses.def: to use someone unfairly for your own advantage
ex: The company exploited its workers.
Some bosses exploit young people.

senses.def: to use something fully to get an advantage
ex: The country exploits its natural gas.

senses.def: the unfair use of other people or things for your own advantage
ex: The report describes the exploitation of child workers.
The exploitation of oil began in 1960.

senses.def: a person who travels to unknown places to find out about them
ex: The explorer reached the South Pole.
Early explorers sailed across the ocean.

senses.def: a sudden, loud and violent burst, for example from a bomb
ex: There was a huge explosion in the factory.
We heard a loud explosion.

senses.def: a sudden large increase in something
ex: There has been an explosion in house prices.

senses.def: able or likely to explode
ex: Gas is highly explosive.
The police found explosive materials.

senses.def: likely to cause sudden anger or trouble
ex: The situation in the city is explosive.

senses.def: a substance that can cause an explosion
ex: The workers used explosives to clear rocks.

senses.def: a product sold to another country, or the selling of such goods
ex: Oil is the country's main export.
Exports rose by five per cent.

senses.def: to sell goods to another country
ex: Japan exports cars all over the world.

senses.def: to show something that was hidden or covered
ex: The storm exposed the old roots.
The newspaper exposed the truth.

senses.def: to let someone experience something harmful or new
ex: Do not expose children to too much sun.

senses.def: a fast train or bus that stops at few places
ex: We took the express to the airport.

senses.def: to show a feeling, idea or opinion in words or actions
ex: She expressed her thanks to the team.
It is hard to express how I feel.

mistake.note: express takes a direct object with no preposition.

senses.def: extremely beautiful and delicate
ex: She wore an exquisite silk dress.
The room has exquisite details.

senses.def: to make something longer or larger, or last longer
ex: They plan to extend the road.
I extended my visa by a month.

senses.def: to cover a certain distance or area
ex: The forest extends for many miles.

senses.def: a new room or part added to a building
ex: They built an extension at the back of the house.

senses.def: extra time allowed for something
ex: I asked for an extension on my essay.

senses.def: a separate phone line inside an office
ex: Please call me on extension 305.

senses.def: covering a large area or including many details
ex: The storm caused extensive damage.
She has extensive knowledge of art.

senses.def: how large, important or serious something is
ex: We do not know the full extent of the damage.
To some extent, I agree.

mistake.note: The fixed phrase is to some extent, not 'in some extent'.

senses.def: the outside part of something, especially a building
ex: The exterior of the house is painted white.
He has a tough exterior but a kind heart.

senses.def: on, from or relating to the outside of something
ex: Use an external hard drive to save your files.
External walls were painted blue.

senses.def: no longer existing, used about animals or plants
ex: Dinosaurs became extinct millions of years ago.
Many species are in danger of becoming extinct.

senses.def: the crime of getting money from someone by using threats
ex: He was arrested for extortion.
The gang used extortion to make money.

senses.def: more than is usual or already there
ex: Can I have an extra blanket?
There is no extra charge.

senses.def: more than usual; especially
ex: Be extra careful on the ice.
You pay extra for delivery.

senses.def: something added that costs more money
ex: Air conditioning is an optional extra.

senses.def: a short piece taken from a book, film or piece of music
ex: We read an extract from the novel.
He played an extract from the song.

senses.def: a strong substance taken from a plant or food
ex: The drink contains lemon extract.

senses.def: to remove or take out something, often with effort
ex: The dentist extracted a tooth.
Oil is extracted from the sea floor.

senses.def: describing activities that students do outside normal lessons
ex: Chess is a popular extracurricular activity at my school.

senses.def: an activity done outside normal school lessons
ex: Her extracurriculars include drama and football.

senses.def: in a way that is very unusual or surprising
ex: The test was extraordinarily difficult.
She is extraordinarily talented.

senses.def: very unusual, surprising or special
ex: She has an extraordinary memory.
What an extraordinary story!

senses.def: very great in degree or strength
ex: The desert has extreme heat.
He took extreme care.

senses.def: very different from what is normal or reasonable
ex: Her views on the subject are extreme.

senses.def: to a very high degree; very
ex: I am extremely tired.
The test was extremely hard.

senses.def: to show a feeling or quality strongly and clearly
ex: She exudes confidence.
He exuded charm.

senses.def: to let a liquid or smell flow out slowly
ex: The tree exudes a sticky liquid.
